Need to search first.I couldn't write any of these notes. I wasn't able to read a single page, so I have nothing sourced to give you.

**What happened:**
1. I first tried to open the Proverbs 7 pages directly: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, the Bible Hub commentaries on verses 4, 14 and 22, and the NET Bible notes. All six were refused because the tool only opens addresses that have already turned up in a search.
2. I then ran searches covering the main commentaries, the tradition-specific sites and the other views. That attempt failed too: the tool said I had run out of calls for this turn, so no results came back. I can't use the other tools to work around this because they have no internet access.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, URLs or summaries of what each tradition teaches. Anything I produced now would be from memory and unsourced.

**Next step:** If you ask again in a new message, the tool limit should reset. I'd search first, then open these pages and give you the full verse-by-verse notes with a URL for each point:
- **Main commentaries:** Enduring Word on Proverbs 7, Precept Austin's Proverbs 7 page, and Bible Hub's verse pages (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Benson and others), especially verses 4, 14, 22–23 and 27.
- **Modern scholarship:** NET Bible notes, mainly on the "peace offerings" in v. 14, the hard-to-translate Hebrew in v. 22 and "Sheol" in v. 27, plus Bible Odyssey on the "strange woman."
- **Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon, and Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition and Desiring God, to check whether any tradition really reads a verse differently.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** New Advent (Church Fathers), Catholic Answers and OCA for any well-known readings, such as the woman as a picture of heresy or idolatry.
